title: Knowledge check: Vue Single-File Components

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Vue Single-File Components”?
options: Expose private credentials in client-side environment variables.
Use create-vue with Vite for new Vue projects, understand the SFC/entry-point roles, and test production builds separately from the dev server.
Use Vue CLI as the primary new-project scaffolder without checking its status.
Edit generated dist assets as the source of truth.
questions.answer_key: Use create-vue with Vite for new Vue projects, understand the SFC/entry-point roles, and test production builds separately from the dev server.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Vue Single-File Components directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Purpose of .vue files”, which practice is most reliable?
options: The entry point creates the Vue app, registers features, and mounts the root component.
Every component must call createApp separately.
The dist/ folder is the editable source of the app.
Vite reads production secrets from client code.
questions.answer_key: The entry point creates the Vue app, registers features, and mounts the root component.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Purpose of .vue files”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Vue Single-File Components” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.
